exposure: augmentation of labour with synthetic oxytocin
cervical dilatation at time of oxytocin infusion
outcome: prevalence of augmentation of labour with synthetic oxytocin
cohort: The study included data from 2,086 women who gave birth in one tertiary urban maternity hospital in Ireland.
finding: The overall prevalence of augmentation of labour with synthetic oxytocin was 18.70%, with nulliparity and private care significantly increasing the odds of augmentation.
mod_finding: Augmentation of labour with synthetic oxytocin was associated with instrument-assisted birth regardless of cervical dilatation at the time of infusion, and showed mixed associations with caesarean section depending on cervical dilatation.
